title: Browser Data & Networking APIs: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before notes on fetch, response handling, aborting requests, browser storage options, IndexedDB basics and URL/URLSearchParams. Covers the mental model, workflow, everyday usage, common mistakes and a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Fetch Mental Model and Options
points: fetch(url, options) returns a Promise<Response> that resolves once headers arrive; the body is a separate stream read later
Options object: method (default GET), headers, body, credentials, mode, cache, signal
POST JSON: fetch(url,{method:'POST',headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify(data)})
Body must be a string, FormData, Blob or URLSearchParams; never pass a raw object (becomes "[object Object]")
credentials: 'same-origin' (default) | 'include' sends cookies cross-origin | 'omit' never sends them

chapters.title: response.ok, Status and Parsing JSON
points: fetch rejects only on network failure or abort; HTTP 404/500 still resolve, so always check response.ok (status 200-299)
Core pattern: const res = await fetch(u); if(!res.ok) throw new Error(res.status); const data = await res.json()
Body parsers: res.json(), res.text(), res.blob(), res.formData(), res.arrayBuffer(); each returns a Promise
A body can be read only once; use res.clone() before reading it a second time (bodyUsed becomes true)
res.json() rejects on empty or invalid JSON (e.g. 204 No Content), so check status or read text() first

chapters.title: AbortController and Timeouts
points: const ctrl = new AbortController(); fetch(url,{signal:ctrl.signal}); ctrl.abort() cancels the request
An aborted fetch rejects with DOMException name 'AbortError'; catch it and ignore it separately from real errors
Timeout shortcut: fetch(url,{signal:AbortSignal.timeout(5000)}) rejects with 'TimeoutError' after 5s
Combine user cancel and timeout: AbortSignal.any([ctrl.signal, AbortSignal.timeout(5000)])
A controller is single-use: once aborted, create a new one per request; in React abort in the effect cleanup to avoid stale responses

chapters.title: localStorage vs sessionStorage vs Cookies
points: localStorage persists until cleared and is shared across tabs of one origin; sessionStorage lasts one tab and is gone when the tab closes
Both are synchronous with ~5MB per origin and string-only values: setItem(k,v), getItem(k) (null if missing), removeItem(k), clear()
Store objects with JSON.stringify and read them back with JSON.parse; a bare object is saved as "[object Object]"
Cookies hold ~4KB and are sent with every HTTP request to the server; options: Expires/Max-Age, Path, Secure, SameSite, HttpOnly
HttpOnly cookies are unreadable by JS, so put auth tokens there; anything in web storage is readable by any XSS script, so never store secrets in it

chapters.title: IndexedDB Basics
points: IndexedDB is an async, transactional, key-value object store for large structured data (objects, Blobs, files); capacity is hundreds of MB or more, far beyond web storage
Workflow: indexedDB.open(name, version) then onupgradeneeded runs createObjectStore(name,{keyPath:'id'}) and createIndex; you can only change the schema there, and only by bumping the version
Reads and writes happen in a transaction: db.transaction('store','readwrite').objectStore('store').put(obj); also add, get, delete, getAll
Its native API is event/callback based (onsuccess, onerror) rather than Promise based, so use a wrapper like idb in real projects
Choose it over localStorage for offline data, large data or queryable data; it is also available in web workers, unlike localStorage

chapters.title: URL, URLSearchParams and Cheat Sheet
points: new URL('/api?q=a', 'https://x.com') parses and builds URLs; properties: origin, pathname, search, hash, searchParams; an invalid URL throws TypeError
URLSearchParams: get(k), getAll(k), has(k), set(k,v) replaces, append(k,v) adds a duplicate, delete(k), toString(); it iterates as [key, value] pairs
Build queries safely with url.searchParams.set('q','a b&c'): it encodes the value for you, so never concatenate strings by hand
encodeURIComponent for a single value; encodeURI for a whole URL; fetch(url) accepts a URL object and URLSearchParams works as a request body

Cheat sheet: check res.ok then await res.json(); signal: AbortSignal.timeout(ms); localStorage = persistent string store; sessionStorage = per tab; HttpOnly cookie = auth; IndexedDB = large async data
